parts.text:
Ask any reptile lover where to find a cold-blooded creature and chances are they will point to a rocky outcrop.

Look

and you might find a snake or lizard basking on a sun-warmed boulder, sheltering in a narrow crevice or even living under a loose surface rock.

For reptiles, these rocks are not simply somewhere to hang out.

Rocky

help reptiles control their body temperature, escape predators and survive harsh winters. They are also a refuge where reptiles can socialise, lay eggs and find food.

Without rocky habitats, many reptile species would

to survive, putting wider ecosystems at risk of collapse. But how many reptile species actually depend on rocky habitats?

Our new study

both to answer this question and identify what threats rock-dwelling species face.

Rocky habitats at risk

Rocky habitats are found on every continent, ranging from cliff faces to outcrops and even areas covered with loose, scattered rocks.

Rocky habitats may seem relatively

compared to forests or other living habitats. In reality, they are easily damaged or destroyed and, once lost, may take centuries or even millenia to reform.

Today, one in five reptile species is at risk of

. Habitat loss is the most pressing threat to reptile populations worldwide.

Rocky areas are under pressure from threats such as mining, quarrying and urbanisation. In the United Arab Emirates, for instance, rapid urban development

the last isolated rock formation known to support the critically endangered Emirati leaf-toed gecko (Asaccus caudivolvulus).

Rock crushing is another problem. It involves using specialised

to turn boulderfields and other rocky habitats into farmland. In Australia, new rock crushing machinery can clear and crush surface rocks at rates of up to one hectare per hour. These methods are increasingly being used in

areas in Western Australia, South Australia and western Victoria, threatening the habitat of several threatened reptile species.

Despite their importance, rocky habitats are often overlooked in conservation plans and
, such as the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s (IUCN) habitat classification system.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Condor conservation illustrates the importance of deciding whose voices shape species protection.
Studying starling murmurations may reveal how spectacular flocking displays change as bird numbers fall.
Rocky habitats support many reptile species but are often overlooked in conservation.
Humidity increases the danger of heatwaves and deserves greater attention in public warnings.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: Despite their importance, rocky habitats are often overlooked in conservation plans and initiatives, such as the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s (IUCN) habitat classification system.

questions.prompt: Why are rocky habitats useful to reptiles?
options: They prevent any other species from entering an ecosystem.

They guarantee a constant temperature in every season.
They help regulate temperature, avoid predators and survive harsh conditions.
